steps.u: We need to split contacts.full_name into first_name and last_name. The contacts table has ~40M rows and the app can't go down. Plan it and start.

steps.a: Doing it in one migration (add columns, UPDATE all rows, drop full_name) would rewrite 40M rows inside one transaction, hold locks and break any app instance still reading full_name during the deploy. I'll use expand-contract instead so every step is online: 1) add nullable columns; 2) app writes both; 3) backfill in batches; 4) app reads the new columns; 5) drop full_name later.

i.content:
-- expand: nullable, no default, so no table rewrite
ALTER TABLE contacts ADD COLUMN first_name text, ADD COLUMN last_name text;

i.old_string: await db.query('UPDATE contacts SET full_name = $2 WHERE id = $1', [id, c.fullName]);
i.new_string:
const { first, last } = splitName(c.fullName);
  await db.query('UPDATE contacts SET full_name = $2, first_name = $3, last_name = $4 WHERE id = $1', [id, c.fullName, first, last]);

i.command: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f db/migrate/20261120_add_name_parts.sql && npm test -- contacts && npx tsx scripts/backfill_name_parts.ts 2>&1 | tail -3

steps.a: I stopped the backfill at id 19,004,999 because replica lag climbed to 41 seconds, which would make read-after-write on the replicas noticeably stale. Current state: columns added (step 1), app writes both full_name and the new columns (step 2), backfill about half done with ~21.1M rows remaining (step 3, resume with --from=19005000 and a longer sleep, e.g. 250 ms, ideally off-peak). Steps 4 (switch reads) and 5 (drop full_name) are not started. Contacts tests pass (23).

reference.summary: Started an online schema change splitting a full name column into first and last names on a 40-million-row table using the expand-contract pattern: added nullable columns, made the app dual-write, and ran a batched resumable backfill. The backfill was paused about halfway because replica lag reached 41 seconds; switching reads and dropping the old column are not done.
facts: The table has about 40M rows and 31 GB
Nullable columns were added without a table rewrite and the repository writes both old and new columns
A batched, resumable backfill in 5,000-row id ranges was written
The backfill stopped at about 19M with about 21.1M rows remaining because replica lag reached 41 s
Switching reads and dropping the old column remain; contacts tests pass

decisions.choice: Use expand-contract instead of a single migration
decisions.reason: a single migration would rewrite 40M rows in one transaction and break instances still reading the old column, and the app cannot go down
replica lag reached 41 seconds, making replica reads stale
